entries.title: Bounded-Radius Definitional d-DNNF Compiler Conjecture
entries.reason: Existentially forgetting the auxiliary variables from the promised polynomial-size d-DNNF yields an ordinary DNNF of no greater size. Explicit polynomial-size CNF families are known to require exponential DNNF size, so the universal compiler cannot exist.
entries.salvage: A descendant must target a representation language not closed under efficient forgetting to ordinary DNNF, weaken full projected equivalence to a narrower property, or restrict the input class.

entries.title: Bounded-Interface Exact Residual Quotient Conjecture
entries.reason: The registered statement omitted coverage, acceptance completeness, rejection soundness, and a decision requirement. An algorithm with no accepting paths satisfies the written class and witness clauses vacuously while deciding nothing.
entries.salvage: A descendant must require a complete quotient DAG covering all assignments, acceptance iff satisfiable, certified rejection for unsatisfiable inputs, and polynomial bounds on the entire computation rather than only merge certificates.
